title: Go to Dark Gethsemane
lyrics_original: Go to dark Gethsemane,
Ye that feel the tempter's power;
Your Redeemer's conflict see,
Watch with Him one bitter hour,
Turn not from His griefs away;
Learn of Jesus Christ to pray.
See Him at the judgment hall,
Beaten, bound, reviled, arraigned;
O the wormwood and the gall!
O the pangs His soul sustained!
Shun not suffering, shame, or loss;
Learn of Christ to bear the cross.
Calvary's mournful mountain climb;
There, adoring at His feet,
Mark that miracle of time,
God's own sacrifice complete.
"It is finished!" hear Him cry;
Learn of Jesus Christ to die.
Early hasten to the tomb
Where they laid His breathless clay;
All is solitude and gloom.
Who has taken Him away?
Christ is risen! He meets our eyes;
Savior, teach us so to rise.

bible_verses.english: Then he said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch with me.” He went forward a little, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not as I desire, but as you desire.”
An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him. Being in agony he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.
But he was wounded for our transgressions. He was bruised for our iniquities. The chastisement of our peace was on him; and with his stripes we are healed.

devotional.prayer_english: Lord Jesus, thank You for enduring the bitterness of Gethsemane and the pain of the cross for my sake. When temptation or suffering weighs heavy on my heart, teach me to pray as You prayed, surrendering my will to the Father. Help me not to shrink back from hardship, but to draw near to You in quiet trust. Grant me the grace to remain faithful in every dark hour, knowing Your love has already won the victory. Amen.

devotional.reflection_english: "Go to Dark Gethsemane" invites us to step alongside Jesus in His deepest hours of agony and temptation. Rather than turning away from His grief, we are called to behold the cost of our redemption and learn how to pray when darkness surrounds us. In His submission to the Father's will, Christ transforms our own moments of trial into places of profound intimacy with God. May we draw near to Him today, finding courage in His unfailing love.
